subject: Call recap: candidate models to trial + acceptance metrics
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta@beaconhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 05 Dec 2026 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Call recap: candidate models to trial + acceptance metrics

Thanks again for the time today, Marta — good discussion. Quick recap from our side, plus recommended next steps so we can get the trial running this month.

Summary of call
- Use case: Beacon wants an assistant that ingests clinical intake notes and returns structured care recommendations and short patient-facing summaries. High priority: factuality (minimize hallucinations), strict PHI handling, and <300ms median token-latency for single-turn queries under load.
- Current baseline: Beacon’s internal ensemble (proprietary) — internal QA shows 86% exact-match on our sample tasks but suffers from occasional hallucinated medication suggestions.

Redwood recommended candidate models to trial (shortlist)
- Redwood-4B-quant (fast, 8-bit inference profile) — best baseline for latency/cost; expect lower hallucination rate than community 4B families in our benchmarks.
- Llama2-13B (float16) — stronger quality ceiling, higher compute; good for parity checks vs your internal baseline.
- MosaicGPT-J-6B (opt-tuned) — middle ground on cost/quality; useful as a control to see how model family affects hallucination patterns.

Acceptance criteria (what Beacon told us / what we should measure)
1) Factuality threshold: exact-match >= 90% on the curated clinical QA set ("QA_clinical_v1") and hallucination rate <= 2% measured via entity hallucination detection script.
2) Latency: median per-request token latency <= 300ms at 30 qps sustained (with Redwood batching settings tuned as recommended).
3) Safety/PII: zero leakage of patient identifiers in outputs on the sanitized test prompts (we will run a red-team pass).

Attachments included: prompt set (beacon_prompt_set_v1.jsonl), latest bench table (benchmark_results_20261204.csv), and the mutual action plan PDF we sketched (mutual_action_plan_beacon.pdf).

Proposed next steps
- Redwood runs a 2-week trial: we provision a dedicated test pool, run benchmark sweep across the three candidates on your prompt set, and produce a parity report vs your proprietary baseline. (Action owner: Soojin)
- Engineering sync: Marcus and Neha to validate PHI handling / KMS setup (Action owner: Beacon + Redwood infra).
- Decision meeting: compare parity metrics and recommend a rollout candidate; target week of Dec 21 for decision.

If that all looks right, I’ll:
1) share the HubSpot deal/MAp links (below),
2) push test prompts into the trial project, and
3) schedule the infra sync with Marcus/Neha.

Thanks — Soojin

--
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0162
From: Marta Ruiz <marta@beaconhealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 05 Dec 2026 18:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Call recap: candidate models to trial + acceptance metrics

Thanks Soojin — appreciate the clear summary. A couple quick clarifications before we lock dates:  
1) When you say exact-match >= 90%, is that on intent/classification labels or on span-level clinical entity extraction? For us the most important metric is medication and dosing extraction accuracy.
2) For latency, the 300ms is for end-to-end single-turn generation (including Redwood routing)? We have a hard SLO of 350ms for UI-facing interactions.

Also: Alex (cc’d on future threads) will be the engineering lead on the Beacon side; I’m looping him into the infra sync. We can share an initial test payload dump tomorrow.

-Marta

Thanks Marta — quick answers and proposed plan to address the points you raised.

1) Metrics breakdown
- Exact-match: we’ll measure both span-level entity extraction (medication/dose) and intent-level labels. For your requirement we’ll prioritize span-level medication/dosing EM and report both.
- Hallucination detection: we’ll run our entity-hallucination detector and also include a manual spot-check on 200 randomly sampled cases.

2) Latency definition
- Our latency target in the benchmark will be end-to-end median per-request token latency (includes routing + batching + model inference). We will report p50/p90/p99. We’ll tune Redwood batching to meet your 350ms SLO; our goal is to show median <= 300ms under the 30 qps load you described.

Action items we’ll pick up now:
- Redwood: kick off trial project and run initial benchmarks on the three candidate models against beacon_prompt_set_v1.jsonl. Deliverable: benchmark_results_20261204.csv + parity write-up (Action owner: Marissa).
- Infra sync: Marcus/Neha to propose KMS/ingestion checklist and a short-runbook for PHI handling; propose meeting times this week.
- Acceptance thresholds: we’ll produce a short one-page acceptance checklist (EM thresholds, hallucination gating rules, latency SLOs) and include it in the MAp PDF.

I’ve created a HubSpot deal and uploaded the prompt set to the Beacon folder on Drive: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/BEACON-4385 and https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB_example_drive_link

Let us know preferred windows for the infra sync (we have availability Wed/Thu mornings PST).

-Marissa
